Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Billing anomaly — duplicate token counts during Feb 12 outage

Hi Samira,

Thanks for flagging this via support. I wanted to reach out directly — our SRE team detected an incident earlier today (09:02 PST) that caused some API requests to be reprocessed during a brief window, and that behavior likely affected token accounting for a subset of requests.

Immediate notes:
- We're investigating scope and will provide a precise breakdown as soon as the token audit finishes (ETA 6–8 hours).
- We will issue credits/refunds for any verified duplicate charges; you will not be billed for duplicate tokens.
- For transparency, I attached a placeholder invoice you referenced and will send a reconciliation once the audit completes.

Could you confirm the invoice numbers you saw with duplicate lines so we can prioritize the reconciliation?

Apologies for the disruption — I know even small billing surprises disrupt finance workflows. We're treating this as high priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing anomaly — duplicate token counts during Feb 12 outage

Marissa, Rachel, Jonas —

Root cause summary (TL;DR): a retry-suppression race during our rollback path caused a small subset of requests to be enqueued twice when the upstream LB timed out. That resulted in duplicate generation calls and duplicate token accounting for ~0.27% of requests in the 09:02–09:18 PST window.

What we did and next steps:
- Completed token-level reconciliation for Acme's tenant (attached). The CSV lists 1,324 requests in the window; 27 were duplicate-accounted. Reconciled token deltas: -12,430 tokens total.
- Preventive fix: adjusted retry-suppression gating and added a per-request idempotency check in the router (deploy completed 12:47 PST).
- Recompute plan: billing will receive an amended usage CSV and a credit batch file by EOD. If finance needs faster action, we can issue provisional credits and reverse after final reconciliation.

Attachments: token_audit_20260212.csv (stub)

Let me know if you want the raw logs; I can share a redacted subset for compliance.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for your patience. We completed the audit and confirmed duplicate accounting on 27 requests affecting INV-8221 and INV-8222. Summary below: 

- Duplicate tokens identified: 12,430 tokens (net)
- Credit amount: $2,432.00 (applied as a one-time account credit to Acme Logistics; will appear on your next invoice)
- Files provided: reconciled_usage_20260212.csv, token_audit_20260212.csv (attached), redwood-refund-authorization.pdf

What we changed: a fix to retry-suppression logic was deployed at 12:47 PST to prevent re-enqueueing in the rollback path. We also added an idempotency check that compares request IDs at the router layer.

Next steps for you:
- Rachel (cc'd) has prepared an authorization PDF for Procurement. If you confirm receipt, we'll send the credit now and mark the ticket resolved.
- If your finance team prefers a direct invoice correction rather than a credit, reply to this message and Rachel will coordinate a corrected invoice.

Again, I apologize for the friction here. We're running a follow-up postmortem and will share more details (timeline and postmortem summary) with your team by Friday.

Best,
